title: Periodic properties: ionisation reversal, isoelectronic radii, alkali densities and bond strength
summary: Strip electrons off boron and carbon to find where the second-ionisation trend reverses, shrink an isoelectronic series by adding protons, weigh a cubic centimetre of each alkali metal and break H-H against F-F.
subject: Chemistry
subtopics: Successive ionisation enthalpies and cation configurations
Densities of the alkali metals and the Na-K inversion
Bond dissociation enthalpy of the halogens and the F-F anomaly
concepts: The second ionisation removes an electron from the cation, not the atom
A filled subshell in the cation makes the next ionisation expensive
Within an isoelectronic set the radius falls as the nuclear charge rises
Density is a ratio, so a faster-growing volume can outrun a growing mass
Lone-pair repulsion on small atoms weakens a single bond
formulas: radii: Al3+ 53.5 < Mg2+ 72 < Na+ 102 pm (all 10 electrons)
bond enthalpies: H-H 436, Cl-Cl 242, Br-Br 193, F-F 158.8, I-I 151 kJ/mol

methods: Ionisation values taken from primary reference data (Wikipedia element pages, which cite CRC): B 800.6 / 2427.1, C 1086.5 / 2352.6 kJ/mol
The reversal explained structurally, not just numerically: B+ is 1s2 2s2 with a filled penetrating 2s, while C+ is 1s2 2s2 2p1 and loses a shielded 2p electron
The IE2 gap is 74.5 kJ/mol, far outside any measurement uncertainty, so the ordering is not a rounding artefact
All three ions confirmed to hold exactly 10 electrons before their radii were compared, since the trend statement is only meaningful within an isoelectronic set
Shannon six-coordinate radii used throughout: Na+ 102, Mg2+ 72, Al3+ 53.5 pm
Densities cross-checked against element reference pages: K 0.859 g/cm3 at 20 C against Na 0.968, confirming the inversion
Bond enthalpies checked across the whole halogen series: Cl-Cl 242 > Br-Br 193 > F-F 158.8 > I-I 151 kJ/mol, showing fluorine out of place
Distractor audit: (C) and (D) are both correct-sounding generalisations with a famous exception, which is what makes them effective
Answer derived independently first, then cross-checked against a published answer key and worked solution for this paper, which agree on (A) and (B) and quote the same values

Headless-browser run of the finished page: 30 assertions covering the periodic table selector, electron stripping on both elements, the comparison selector, the isoelectronic sweep, both bulk benches, the gate, predictions, theme toggle, clean console and zero horizontal overflow at 390 px and 360 px
verification.note: IIT Roorkee's official key was not retrievable; the published key used for cross-checking is a coaching-institute key that agrees with the independent derivation in every respect.
